deepdive.divline: Dividend Rs.1.50/share (final) + Rs.2.00/share (interim); Free Cash Flow Rs.826cr (100% of PAT); Active M&A in medical (asset purchase closed)

profile.entities: Tube Investments of India Ltd (Parent); CG Power & Industrial Solutions (56%); Shanthi Gears Ltd (70%); TI Clean Mobility Pvt Ltd (Subs)
profile.subseg: Engineering Products; Metal Formed Products; Electric Mobility; Medical Devices; Gears & Power Transmission
profile.themes: EV HCV Scale-up; Supply Chain Vertical Integration; Medical Device M&A; Railway Product Certification

assumptions: EV supplier bottleneck fully resolved by Q2FY27, enabling full volume ramp
Medical segment grows 15-20% YoY throughout FY27
Commodity cost pass-through lag of 1-2 quarters normalizes by Q2FY27
Fuel cost inflation persists but partially mitigated by negotiations
Standalone capex Rs.300-350cr and subsidiary capex ~Rs.300cr incurred evenly
No major one-off gains or losses; tax rate ~25% consistent with history
CG Power and Shanthi Gears maintain Q4FY26 run-rate with modest growth

projection.rationale: Revenue dips sequentially from Q4FY26 peak due to seasonality and EV ramp still in early stages, but grows YoY on CDMO start and medical 15-20% growth. OPM improves slightly from Q4FY26 as supplier bottleneck eases, though commodity lag persists.

Sequential growth driven by EV deployment acceleration and CDMO commercial production. OPM reaches 10% as commodity pass-through catches up and higher-margin EV/medical mix improves, though railway tender pressure remains.
Revenue growth moderates but remains positive on sustained EV and medical momentum. OPM stable near 10% as fuel cost inflation is negotiated and MFP margins remain under pressure from Hyundai mix.

Year-end push with full EV potential realized and CDMO at scale. YoY growth moderates against high Q4FY26 base. OPM remains range-bound as capex depreciation starts impacting, offset by operating leverage.

sources: management commentary on EV, medical, CDMO, margins

bull_bear.body: Dividend Rs.1.50/share (final) + Rs.2.00/share (interim); Free Cash Flow Rs.826cr (100% of PAT); Active M&A in medical (asset purchase closed).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: EV financing availability for fleet operators; Charging infrastructure deployment delays; Railway approval timelines; Commodity price volatility lag; Geopolitical impact on medical exports (Middle East).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Bullish on volume growth despite macro headwinds; Pragmatic on cost pass-through lags; Confident in supply chain fixes (BIW in-house); Strategic patience on railway/tech shifts.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: EV three-wheeler volume miss was a deliberate short-term hit to solve a multi-year supplier bottleneck by acquiring the facility, enabling immediate ramp-up in April/May; Shift in long-haul EV strategy from battery-swap to high-capacity fast-charging based on China trends, though swap retained for ports.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Engineering: Rev Rs.1,495cr (+21.6% YoY), PBIT Rs.176cr; Metal Formed: Rev Rs.421cr (+4.5% YoY), PBIT Rs.35cr (-10% YoY) impacted by Hyundai muted growth/railway tender margins; Mobility (EV): Rev Rs.208cr (+14.9% YoY), PBIT Rs.4cr (flat); Volumes: 87 Big Trucks, 241 SCV, 1,176 Three-wheelers; Medical: Rev Rs.246cr (+0.8% YoY), PBIT Rs.16cr.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply chain bottleneck resolved by in-house takeover | Tube Investments of India Ltd | beneficiary | High | BIW facility acquisition removes structural cap on 3W volumes; immediate ramp expected in Q1 FY27. |
| Commodity inflation lag and railway tender margin pressure | Shanthi Gears Ltd | loser | Med | Revenue declined 11.8% YoY; margin compression in gear segment due to product mix and slower industrial demand. |
| High deployment capex and charging infra gaps | CG Power & Industrial Solutions | beneficiary | High | Strong 25% revenue growth and 27% PBIT growth provide cash flow cushion for group; benefits from broader power capex cycle unrelated to EV infra delays. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: Commodity price inflation passed through with 1-2 quarter lag; Fuel cost inflation immediate challenge being negotiated; MFP margins pressured by low-margin railway tenders and Hyundai volume mix.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Standalone Capex Rs.300-350cr; Subsidiary Capex ~Rs.300cr; TI Medical growth 15-20% YoY; EV deployment ramping in Q1/Q2 FY27 post-infrastructure financing resolution; CDMO commercial production starts Q1 FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: EV Heavy Trucks: Strong order book cited (specific value undisclosed); Deployment pending financing/charging infra; Three-wheeler order flow recovering post-supply fix.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Railway Vande Bharat component certification (2-3 quarters away); CDMO plant commissioning (Naidupet); IV Cannula asset acquisition (Ambala) starting production Q1/Q2 FY27; EV long-haul battery swap vs. fast-charge technology pivot.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: TII delivered robust consolidated growth (Revenue +21% YoY) driven by CG Power and core Engineering, while standalone EV mobility faced temporary supply constraints now resolved via in-house capacity capture. The strategic pivot to internalize body-in-white production and pending railway certifications positions FY27 for accelerated volume recovery despite near-term commodity cost headwinds.

open.item: In-house battery packing (Manesar plant) is to be operational towards the end of FY26, which will bring EV component prices down further.
TI Clean Mobility EV volumes for FY26 will definitely be higher than the previous year.
Small commercial vehicle network to go from 2 fully operational dealers to 25 across the country, and e-tractor from 4 to about 25 fully operational dealerships before the end of FY26.
open.promised: 25 dealers each for SCV and e-tractor dealers

open.item: The new Nasik plant adds about 7-8% incremental capacity to the engineering division, roughly 4,000 tonnes per month.
open.promised: 4000 tonnes per month; 7-8% incremental engineering capacity tonnes per month

open.item: EV/clean mobility capex of close to INR300 crores is planned for next financial year across all four businesses.

Having taken over the body-in-white supplier's facility, management is confident of resolving the body-in-white bottleneck by and large by the end of Q1FY27, with April and May ramp-up already at targeted levels.
open.promised: issue resolved by end of quarter text

open.item: After a body-in-white supplier issue cut Q4 three-wheeler output to 50% of potential, management is confident of returning to normal production capacity by the end of Q1FY27.
open.promised: back to normal production capacity text

open.item: The L3 foray is only seeded in select markets for product/price testing; a call on the product's future and GTM strategy will be taken basis feedback over the next quarter or so.
CG Power is recruiting one or two key people to drive growth of the services business, with the team expected to be on board in Q1 FY2027 before growth starts.
open.promised: team on board by Q1FY2027 date

open.item: The CDMO plant is under final commissioning and commercial production will start from the Naidupet facility next quarter.
open.promised: commercial production starting next quarter date

open.item: The Medicura facility at Ambala (IV cannula asset purchase) is closed; plant approvals and team hiring are to be completed in Q1-Q2FY27, after which commercial production is expected to start.
open.promised: commercial production start after Q1-Q2 approvals date

open.item: TI Clean Mobility has a good order book for heavy electric trucks and expects to deploy these trucks in Q1 and Q2 of FY27 once financing and charging infrastructure bottlenecks are untangled.
open.promised: deployment in Q1 and Q2 text

open.item: The new engineering plant in the West is deferred and expected to be delayed by six to nine months due to machine supplier challenges.
The CRSS plant at Nasik is ramping up and is expected to reach 100% utilisation by end of FY27 or the middle of FY28.
A rough-cut estimate of around Rs.300 Crores is planned to be invested into subsidiaries (TICMPL EV business and TI Medical) in FY27.
FY27 capex in the standalone core business is guided at around Rs.300 Crores to Rs.350 Crores.
Management reiterated confidence in growing the wound care / suture business at 15% to 20%.

open.horizon: two to three quarters from Q1FY27
open.item: Railway product development is complete but customer approvals with Government of India for Vande Bharat coaches are pending; management expects some visible progress two to three quarters from now.
European demand is weak and MFPD exports to Europe are a drag; any EU FTA benefit will come with a lag of around 12 to 15 months and non-tariff barriers such as CBAM remain a challenge.
Tube facilities in the Western region have reached about 30% capacity utilisation and management is hopeful of 100% utilisation by the middle of the next financial year.

revisions.item: Management reiterated confidence in double-digit growth (including on EBITDA) for the standalone business, subject to export headwinds.
Management is hopeful of delivering 20% year-on-year growth in TI Medical going forward, aided by the newly acquired IV cannula business.

verdicts.note: Full-year MFPD margin sits at the low end of the band but Q4 fell below it; Mukesh Ahuja: 'MFPD is going a bit slow' on railways tender profitability and muted Hyundai volumes. [±10% rule]

wtt.summary: 79% guidance hit (7 chains); 1/5 projects on-time; 2 guidance revision(s); 8 expired; 12% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Confident and bullish on demand and new-vertical growth, with management explicitly owning misses — the Q4 three-wheeler volume hit from the body-in-white supplier (only 50% of potential output), the repeatedly delayed railway scale-up, sluggish MFPD, and the muted medical devices exports.
